attempts.entry_title: Dendritic spikes and back-propagation in CA1 neurons (Park, Wong-Campos et al. 2025)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Park, Wong-Campos et al. (2025) on dandiset 001266, which holds the example recordings of the paper's figures (raw voltage imaging movies of CA1 pyramidal neurons in slices with their stimulus and patch clamp channels). It counts bAPs and dSpikes in the neuron of Figs. 2 and 3, the step, wide-field and drug examples, measures the plateau examples, and checks the optical recording against patch clamp. A second notebook runs the paper's published NEURON model for its model claims. The pooled samples behind most of the paper's statistics are not in the dandiset.

outcomes.statement: In the Fig. 2 neuron, stimulation of proximal oblique dendrites evoked two somatic spikes per trial; in most trials the distal dendrites showed only an attenuated copy, and in 8 of 54 trials a single rapid dSpike, always on the second somatic spike.
outcomes.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 1; Figure 2a, 2c
outcomes.quote: Each stimulus evoked two spikes at the soma ... in some cases (8 of 54 trials), the dendrites produced a single rapid spike ... the dendritic excitations always emerged from the second somatic spike, never the first
outcomes.notes: 8 of 54 trials carry a dSpike under both filter readings, with the claims file's 5 s.d. threshold and with 4 s.d., distal region beyond 300 µm; no dSpike follows the first somatic spike of a trial. The statement says more than the criterion tests, and that part does not hold: 7 to 10 trials have three somatic spikes, not two, and 5 to 7 of the 8 dSpikes ride on the third spike; each dSpike is on the last spike of its trial. With the region cut at 400 µm the Butterworth reading gives 6.

dSpike threshold at the first minimum of a Gaussian kernel density (Scott bandwidth) of the distal amplitudes above its failure mode (the lowest density peak at least a quarter as high as the highest), with interpolated FWHM < 5 ms. outcomes.statement: Spike amplitudes have a unimodal distribution at the soma and a bimodal one in the distal dendrite.
outcomes.source: Results, Distal dendritic depolarization favors dendritic spikes, paragraph 1; Figure 2b

outcomes.statement: Optical recording at 1 kHz detected every spike up to 90 Hz with no false positives or negatives (7 cells, 2212 spikes), with a single-trial noise-equivalent voltage of 1.2 ± 0.5 mV (2.5 ± 0.8 mV at 2 kHz) and sensitivity of about 12% dF/F per 100 mV.

outcomes.notes: Sensitivity is 11.7 ± 2.9% per 100 mV at 1 kHz (10.8 ± 3.5% at 2 kHz), within 12 ± 1.2 on average. The noise-equivalent voltage is 3.5 ± 0.5 mV (reading a) and 3.3 ± 0.9 mV (b) at 1 kHz against 1.2 ± 0.5, and 11.4 and 5.2 mV at 2 kHz against 2.5 ± 0.8. At 1 kHz, 6 of 1106 electrical spikes have no optical match and 19 optical spikes have no electrical one; at 2 kHz, 254 of 1159 are missed and 385 added. The two rates together hold 2265 electrical spikes, close to the paper's 2212. Counting an electrical spike only after the membrane repolarized below -30 mV (largest rate 91 Hz, against 333 and 263 Hz with the 3 ms rule) gives 1105 spikes with 5 missed and 19 added at 1 kHz, and 1107 with 189 missed and 372 added at 2 kHz, so the false detections are not an artefact of the electrical count. Two NEV variants were added. Reading (a) in the quietest 1 s window after the first second gives 2.1 ± 0.6 mV at 1 kHz and 3.4 ± 1.1 mV at 2 kHz. With the Methods' maximum-likelihood pixel weighting it gives 1.9 ± 0.6 and 2.5 ± 0.5 mV (in the first second 3.5 ± 0.7 and 7.6 ± 3.8; reading b 3.2 ± 0.9 and 4.3 ± 0.7), so the 2 kHz value falls within 2.5 ± 0.8 and the 1 kHz value stays above 1.2 ± 0.5; the weights lower the sensitivity to 8.1 ± 2.2% at 1 kHz, and 8 spikes are missed and 20 added at 1 kHz (181 and 297 at 2 kHz). The false detections fail the criterion's zero under every reading, so the outcome does not depend on the NEV.

The Methods' maximum-likelihood weighting ("the fluorescence at each pixel was correlated with the whole-field average fluorescence. Pixels that showed stronger correlation to the mean were preferentially weighted", Methods, Extracting fluorescence from movies) is shown as a variant, each pixel weighted by its regression slope on the whole-field mean over its residual variance, both from frame-to-frame differences so that bleaching does not enter (a choice made here; the paper gives no detail).
NEV reading (a) uses the first second, as before; the quietest 1 s window after it (least variance of the membrane potential) is shown as a variant.
Optical spikes use the claims file's 5 s.d. rule on the high-passed trace; the paper set its threshold by hand.

findings.statement: The paper's Supplementary Software 1 does not run as published: run_morphology.py calls FullCA1Model(channel_params, morphology_file), while FullCA1Model requires a third argument, ka_cutoff (run_simulation.py passes 100). Its cheriff.mod carries non-ASCII characters that NEURON 9 rejects. With these fixed, its step simulation at the soma gives success, success, success, success, failure at 500 µm, not the failure, success, success, failures of Fig. 4f. Its phase-diagram sweeps (Plot_Phase_Diagrams.m grids, 429 runs) give the motif in 11, 17 and 0 cells, none at the Table 1 parameters, where the matrices published in the same zip give 51, 48 and 88, including every Table 1 cell. FullCA1Model registers a per-step callback that outlives the model, so runs in one process slow down and can affect each other.

The dandiset holds the example recordings of the figures (the 83 rows of the Source Data index, 84 files), not the pooled samples behind the paper's statistics: the 17 neurons of Fig. 3, the 43 branches of Fig. 4b, the 28 cells of Fig. 5b, the drug series of Figs. 6 and S16 to S18, the temperature series, the patch recordings of Fig. S1 and the calibration series of Figs. S3 to S5. 29 of the 55 claims cannot be tested for this reason.

The files hold only raw camera movies and DAQ channels. They carry no pixel size, no structural (2P or HiLo) or eYFP images, no stimulus masks, and no regions of interest, so distances from the soma, stimulus positions and the user-drawn regions of the paper cannot be recovered from the files. The pixel size used here (0.65 µm) is from the Methods.

Every file is its own subject: subject_id is the file name (81 subjects for 84 files), date_of_birth is 1900-01-01 and sex is U. Animals and cells can be told apart only through the file names (for example PP070-P16-Cell2).

Three recordings are deposited twice with identical sizes and first frames: sub-153924PP070-P27-Cell1-soma-step-5ms (one copy named without a session), sub-000919PP070-P17-V2-11-freq-opto and sub-000820PP070-P17-V2-11-freq-opto-2khz (two copies each, with different obj- suffixes).

Camera frames are 1.03 ms apart (971 Hz; 1.04 ms in one file) where the paper states 1 kHz, and 0.52 ms (1923 Hz) where it states 2 kHz. The movie and the DAQ record span the same time, so the timestamps are consistent; the stated rates are rounded.

The camera series has "no description", and the DAQ channels are named only by short labels that differ between files for the same signal (the EFS trigger is stim1, stim1 (distal), EC, EC_elec or EC_stim). The amplifier gains are given only in the dandiset description, not in the files.

File names and figure legends name stimulus sites differently: the Fig. 2 legend's "D1 stim" is the file named D3, and the Fig. 3 legend's D2 is the file named D4 (its bAP count, 84, matches the legend's 49 + 35). The Source Data index resolves the first; counts resolve the second.

In the Fig. 2 recording 7 to 10 of the 54 trials have three somatic spikes, where the paper says each stimulus evoked two, and most dSpikes ride on the third spike, where the paper says they always emerged from the second.

Question for the paper's authors: what somatic spike threshold, dSpike threshold and distal region (its far end along the dendrite) were used for the bAP and dSpike counts of Figs. 2 to 4 and S8 to S18? The Methods say the thresholds were set by hand and the region was typically beyond 300 µm. Here a somatic threshold of 5 robust s.d. misses spikes in bursts (139 to 150 against the legend's 167 and 170 bAPs), and the counts for Fig. 3f move from 46 to 51 of 54 when the region stops at 400 µm. In several example recordings (the Fig. S15 file beyond 300 µm, the TTX baseline under the median filter, the Ni2+ file of Fig. S18g) the density of the distal amplitudes has no minimum above its failure mode, so no trough threshold exists. In the file of the Fig. 3 legend's D2, the first-bAP count is within tolerance under one high-pass filter and just outside it under the other (32 and 31 of 54, tolerance 31.5 to 38.5).

Question for the paper's authors: how was dF_ref taken when bAPs come in bursts during a 20 ms stimulus, and over what range and with what amplitude measure was the length constant of Fig. 2h fitted? With the reference 10 to 20 ms after each spike (Fig. 1d legend) the normalized profiles rise near the stimulated branch and per-spike exponential fits fail or give 54 or about 1400 µm; raw amplitudes give 356 µm.

Question for the paper's authors: over what window were the AUCs of Figs. 5 and 6 integrated? Up to the end of the cumulative rise, a single bAP with EFS gives ratios above 2 at two timings in the one cell available; to the end of the epoch, the single-stimulus areas are near zero and no ratio exceeds 2.

Question for the paper's authors: how was the noise-equivalent voltage of Fig. S2 defined, and on which pixels (weighted or not)? With the unweighted cell region it is 3.3 to 3.5 mV at 1 kHz here, against 1.2 ± 0.5 mV.

Question for the paper's authors: which pixels and what preprocessing went into the PCA of Fig. S7b? On the stimulus-triggered pixel waveforms of the Fig. 3a recording the first five components hold 22 to 30% of the variance when the waveforms are centred, 39 to 58% when only each pixel's baseline is removed, and 100% on raw counts, where the first component is the resting image.

entries.title: Dendritic spikes and back-propagation in CA1 neurons (Park, Wong-Campos et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Park, Wong-Campos et al. (2025) on dandiset 001266, which holds the example recordings of the paper's figures (raw voltage imaging movies of CA1 pyramidal neurons in slices with their stimulus and patch clamp channels). It counts bAPs and dSpikes in the neuron of Figs. 2 and 3, the step, wide-field and drug examples, measures the plateau examples, and checks the optical recording against patch clamp. A second notebook runs the paper's published NEURON model for its model claims. The pooled samples behind most of the paper's statistics are not in the dandiset.
